title: Browser-based 3D fab twin + open equipment catalog +MIMAC scheduling benchmark
author: W
text:
jinjiefan
New member

I've been building SemiconFab (semiconfab.org) — a browser-based 300mm cleanroom twin (Three.js) with AMHS, MES/SPC/YMS panels and fault scenarios, plus an open catalog of 121 real OEM tools under a 7-layer JSON schema. Every catalog field carries a provenance tier (vendor_confirmed → synthetic) so you can see what's datasheet-solid and what's estimated. Only 7 records are fully verified so far; 114 are drafts awaiting dimensions — the site funnels visitors to submit corrections via GitHub PR.

There's also MIMAC-2026, a synthetic benchmark for fab scheduling research (18 tool groups, 217 machines, dispatching/AMHS/PM tasks, FIFO/SPT/EDD/CR baselines, runnable Python simulator).

Code is source-available: github.com/jinjiefan2020/SemiconFab. The twin is currently teaching-grade visualization, not an industrial twin — less equipments than real fab and the site labels what's illustrative.

Question for the fab engineers here: is field-level provenance useful in practice, or would you rather see a smaller catalog with only verified data? And what equipment data is hardest to find publicly?
